sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AI Agents for Beginners is a free Microsoft course on building AI agents. Its 18 lessons each have a written lesson, a short video and Python code samples, covering design patterns, tool use, agentic RAG, multi-agent systems, memory, protocols and production.
sixtySeconds.problem: Getting started with agents means learning many new patterns and frameworks at once. This course breaks them into standalone lessons you can take in any order, with runnable notebooks for each.
whoFor: Beginners building their first AI agents
Students and educators wanting a free course
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a well-produced, free agent course with videos and code. The samples use Microsoft Foundry, which needs an Azure account; some also support other OpenAI-compatible providers.
requirements: An Azure subscription and Microsoft Foundry project for the code samples

overview: The course has 18 lessons: intro to agents, agentic frameworks, design patterns, tool use, agentic RAG, trustworthy agents, planning, multi-agent, metacognition, agents in production, agentic protocols (MCP, A2A and NLWeb), context engineering, agent memory, Microsoft Agent Framework, computer use agents, deploying scalable agents, local AI agents and securing agents.

Each lesson has a README, a short video for most lessons, and Jupyter notebooks named *-python-agent-framework.ipynb. The code uses Microsoft Agent Framework with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service V2, so you need a Foundry project with a deployed model such as gpt-5-mini.

The repository includes translations into 50+ languages, which makes it large; the README gives a sparse clone that skips them. GitHub Codespaces is recommended to avoid big local downloads, and there is a Discord for help.
